newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan expects benchmark index warrants to delist.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan expects benchmark index warrants to delist.

text.p: Taiwan's securities watchdog said on Friday it expected two Hong Kong-listed call warrants linked to the island's stock index to delist because they had not received permission from the Taiwan Stock Exchange.
"The two Hong Kong-listed Taiwan index warrants should be delisted soon," Hsu Yung-pang, deputy chairman of Taiwan's Securities and Futures Commission, told Reuters by telephone.
Hsu said one of the organisations that launched the unauthorised warrants, Union Bank of Switzerland has bought back over 97 percent of its shares.
The other group, Peregrine Derivatives Ltd, also was buying back its own shares, Hsu said.
"Union Bank's shares will soon be delisted after it completed its buying, and Peregrine should follow the same steps," he said.
Peregrine Derivatives and Union Bank on Wednesday listed their issued warrants, based on Taiwan's weighted index, on the Hong Kong exchange, sparking protests from the Taiwan Stock Exchange.
The Taiwan Stock Exchange on Wednesday voiced "serious concern and objection" over Peregrine's and Union Bank's warrant issues.
Securities officials said the exchange could take legal actions against the two Hong Kong firms for a host of violations that included copyright and trademark infringements.
"The index is Taiwan Stock Exchange's proprietary product; no one should use it without its consent," the commission's Hsu said. The commission supervises the Taiwan Stock Exchange.
Taiwan had said it did not plan to introduce warrants linked to the island's benchmark index, but would launch warrant issues based on more than 20 Taiwan firms in June.
Commission officials have said Taiwan would not allow outsiders to use the index because such an access would cause the market to become volatile.
